findings.passage: I voted against this measure for several reasons. This bill, which will likely become law, seeks to remedy a problem that simply does not exist in Pennsylvania. Voter fraud incidents in the commonwealth are isolated and rare.
findings.note: March 2012 newsletter under her name about the Senate-passed photo ID bill that requires an approved photo ID each time a voter goes to the polls. She says she voted against it, and gives the view that fraud is rare.

findings.passage: At a time when we are facing a budget deficit and subsequent proposed state budget cuts to important programs and services, we simply cannot afford a voter ID law.
findings.note: Same newsletter. Cost argument: estimated at least $4 million to help people without state photo ID get one.

findings.passage: Voting is a right. It should not be an endurance test.
findings.note: Closing lines of the same newsletter, after describing an elderly voter who would have had to cast a provisional ballot without photo ID.

findings.passage: But starting this November, every voter will be required to show a valid form of identification in order to vote. If you do not have a valid form of identification, the state will provide one to you at no cost.
findings.note: Constituent newsletter (dated from the file name and the reference to the next day's primary) explaining the new law and offering her staff's help in getting a free state ID. It lists acceptable IDs and how to apply for a free ID.

findings.passage: “The judge’s decision was a fair ruling, in light of the confusion about the law among voters and administration officials alike over the past few months,” Schwank said.
findings.note: News release on the Commonwealth Court injunction that let voters vote without photo ID in the November 2012 election.
